after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $t(t-2),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit.

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $t-2$, and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t-2} & = \\ \frac{t-2}{t-2}\cdot \frac{1}{t}-\frac{t}{t}\cdot \frac{1}{t-2} & = \\ \frac{t-2}{(t-2)t}-\frac{t}{t(t-2)} & = \\ \frac{t-2-t}{(t-2)t} & = \\ -\frac{2}{(t-2)t} & \end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $2=\frac{2}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{1-x}{1-x}\cdot \frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2(1-x)}{1-x}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(1-x)}{1-x}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2(1-x)+(3-x)}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2-2x+3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{5-3x}{1-x}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: With common denominator (2x+1)(y+1), the numerator is 4x(y+1)-2y(2x+1)=4xy+4x-4xy-2y=4x-2y. Thus option b is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $(2x+1)(y+1),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $y+1,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $2x+1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x}{2x+1}-\frac{2y}{y+1} & = \\ \frac{y+1}{y+1}\cdot \frac{4x}{2x+1}-\frac{2x+1}{2x+1}\cdot \frac{2y}{y+1} & = \\ \frac{4x(y+1)}{(2x+1)(y+1)}-\frac{(2x+1)2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4x(y+1)-(2x+1)2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4xy+4x-4xy-2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & = \\ \frac{4x-2y}{(2x+1)(y+1)} & \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{a}{a}\cdot \frac{3}{1}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{3a}{a}+\frac{2}{a}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a}{a}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{3a+2}{a}\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\frac{3a}{a}+\frac{2}{a} & = \\ \frac{3a+2}{a}\end{aligned}
